witnesses.title: Genuine owned token retains mutable contents
witnesses.caller_stage: parseOwnedJsonBody -> readOwnedJson; no connected production native execution
witnesses.producer_outcome: Parser stores original buffer, decoded text and parsed object by reference; freezes token only.
witnesses.consumer_outcome: ownedJsonText(token)=="{"a":"old"}"; ownedJsonValue(token)=={a:"new"}; readOwnedJson(token).bytes==zero-filled bytes. Token remains genuine.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Comments promise controlled parsed data as produced. Identity proves parser issuance, not immutable contents; readonly is compile-time. No public request bug is established.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: Before content-attested execution claims, keep mutable record/buffer private and return protected derivatives, or explicitly narrow authority to issuance. Preserve original parser semantics.
negative_acceptance_gates: Retained reader buffer and returned value/record must not silently rewrite authoritative data.
No adopt(unknown); token freezing alone is insufficient.

witnesses.authority_expectation: digest_node explicitly promises identifying echo, not content hash; no cryptographic/privacy contract chosen.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: Keep echo scope. An actual identity consumer must define byte/value/order/presence identity and disclosure policy before selecting a hash. No generic hash layer follows from this name.
negative_acceptance_gates: Never use root echo for dedupe/signatures.
Future content identity changes with nested scalar; privacy claim must not echo plaintext/keys.

Decimal min/max similarly fails fieldPlan copy. Without private seam first failure is missing-provenance.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Public defaults permit Decimal carriers. Prepared copy rejects nonplain prototypes deliberately; genuine schema lineage is separate from private preparation provenance.

negative_acceptance_gates: Decimal default/bound and nested/array decimal defaults admit or explicitly abstain.
No arbitrary class adoption; repeated resolution and public default identity remain separately qualified.

witnesses.title: Duplicate exact entries select first natively, last after reconstruction
witnesses.status: direct ABI contract mismatch outside host profile
witnesses.caller_stage: Raw exact_call decode-value money; no decode-value in TS six-op table
witnesses.producer_outcome: decode_input accepts duplicate tuples; native read_key finds first minor. check_shape finds no extra keys.
witnesses.consumer_outcome: Native returns {ok:true,value:{t:"money",minor:"1",currency:"USD"}}. Input reconstruct uses Object.fromEntries -> {minor:"2",currency:"USD"}; public money decoder returns minor=2n.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Transport header requires unique keys but code does not enforce it. Host tag(Object.entries) emits unique keys; ordinary host JSON.parse duplicates use last-wins. Not a general production JSON duplicate bug.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: Enforce declared unique-key admission before core guards, or choose/qualify common duplicate semantics. Existing hygiene contract supports rejection without new policy.
negative_acceptance_gates: Raw duplicate minor/currency/kind must reject under hygiene or have common declared result.
Do not replay ordinary JSON duplicate spelling as this ABI tuple witness.

witnesses.title: Astral diagnostic cut has different UTF16 units
witnesses.caller_stage: public int decode vs raw native decode-value int; valid transport, malformed int content
witnesses.producer_outcome: TS SchemaError(name=SchemaError,kind=schema,message="schema validation failed with 1 violation(s)"); violation path=[],code=format,message="int is malformed",expected="canonical int64 decimal string".
witnesses.consumer_outcome: actual differs: TS UTF16 [34]+[97]*62+[55357]+[46]*3; native [34]+[97]*62+[46]*3. Native returns {ok:false,violations:[...]} separately; Rust deliberately backs cut down to 63 units.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Legacy truncate slices 64 UTF16 units; native strings cannot hold the sliced lone high surrogate. Source acknowledges exclusion; finite vectors avoiding it cannot prove complete payload parity. Exact error bytes remain unresolved compatibility policy (vv.errors-prose/vv.string-diagnostics); this is a parity limitation, not authority to adopt a new message policy.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: Keep explicit exclusion until an admitted diagnostic carrier preserves exact UTF16 or requirement changes. Error wrapper projection is separate.
negative_acceptance_gates: Include astral pairs crossing unit64; compare units and optional field presence.
Never normalize diagnostic Unicode for comparison or extend scalar finite receipts.

witnesses.title: Lone surrogate produces host codec error but native transport refusal
witnesses.caller_stage: owned JSON/public codec vs raw exact String; structural frame remains separate
witnesses.producer_outcome: Host JSON.parse accepts UTF16 [55296]; public int decoder gives format violation, actual JSON quoted string "\ud800".
witnesses.consumer_outcome: Rust String parser refuses unpaired surrogate before codec: {ok:false,transport:"invalid JSON: <serde error>"}. Exact parser message/position not executed, not invented. Separate frame {t:"text",units:[55296]} preserves it with budgets.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Host UTF16 and exact Rust UTF8 String are different admitted domains; structural availability does not constitute execution bridge. Exact error bytes remain unresolved compatibility policy (vv.errors-prose/vv.string-diagnostics); this is a parity limitation, not authority to adopt a new message policy.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: Retain explicit lossless-string domain limit; broad parity would require owner-approved UTF16 carrier. No replacement U+FFFD or imaginary connected validator.
negative_acceptance_gates: Lone high/low surrogates plus paired astral controls.
Transport refusal and expected scalar violations must remain separate outcomes.

witnesses.title: Opaque JSON preserves order rather than canonical bytes
witnesses.status: identity contract clarification, no public defect
witnesses.caller_stage: public json codec -> caller JSON.stringify; no values content-hash consumer
witnesses.producer_outcome: Both numeric-free objects are accepted; encodeJsonValue copies Object.keys order without canonicalization.
witnesses.consumer_outcome: Stringifying encoded first gives {"b":"x","a":"y"}; second gives {"a":"y","b":"x"}. Numeric-index keys additionally obey JS integer-index ordering.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Opaque JSON explicitly preserves order; broad "every value has exactly one encoding" cannot establish canonical bytes for json. No order-insensitive identity chosen.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: Qualify canonical shape vs bytes. Future hash consumer must declare byte identity or semantic/order identity; do not sort opaque JSON by inference.
negative_acceptance_gates: Never substitute value equality for byte equality.
Preserve safe own __proto__, number rejection and enumeration order.

witnesses.title: Native codec violations disappear at backend projection
witnesses.caller_stage: Raw native decode-value reachable through wasmBackend; tsBackend has no corresponding entry
witnesses.producer_outcome: Native {ok:false,violations:[{path:[],code:"type",message:"int has the wrong wire type",expected:"canonical int64 decimal string",actual:"null"}]}; public TS decode throws SchemaError with that payload.
witnesses.consumer_outcome: wasmBackend.call("decode-value",["int",null]) instead throws ValueError(name=ValueError,kind=value,code=invalid-construction,message="native decode violations on decode-value"); payload fields discarded.
witnesses.authority_expectation: Native violations and public SchemaError are different layers. Current scalar host parity cannot be inferred from raw payload correctness or six-op receipt.
witnesses.required_fix_or_decision: For a selected native codec cut, qualify owning public projection of ordered violations; until then advertise raw native payload only.
negative_acceptance_gates: Compare complete wrapper, ordered violations and absent/present expected/actual.
No six-op credit for decode/encode/native validators.
